newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran warns of Afghan crisis reaching Central Asia.
newsitem.headline: Iran warns of Afghan crisis reaching Central Asia.

text.p: Iran expressed concern on Friday over the crisis in Afghanistan boiling over to neighbouring Central Asian states, Tehran radio reported.
"It is natural for us to be concerned that, God forbid, this (Afghan) turmoil would spread to Central Asia," Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told the state-run radio.
Central Asian states shared Iran's concern, said Velayati who was speaking upon return from a lightning tour of the region and India.
Velayati blamed "foreign provocation and inducement" for the war in Afghanistan.
Shi'ite Moslem Iran recognises the government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, driven out of the capital Kabul by the radical Sunni Taleban militia.
Iranian media have accused Pakistan of setting up the Taleban with backing from the United States and funding from Saudi Arabia to counter Iran's influence in the region.
Iran has condemned what it calls foreign meddling in Afghanistan and called on warring factions to seek a power-sharing agreement.
